citations.quote: Assume countable choice and let $n\ge1$. Fourier transformation on Schwartz space extends uniquely to a surjective complex-linear isometry $\mathcal F_2:L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$. It preserves the first-variable-linear inner product, and hence is unitary.
Assume countable choice. The Fourier transform is a topological automorphism of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, with $\mathcal F^2=R$ and $\mathcal F^{-1}=R\mathcal F$, where $Rf(x)=f(-x)$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $n\ge1$ and
$s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ to be the normed-space completion
of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ with the positive-definite norm
$q_s(u)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat u\|_2$ from
[[def-bessel-potential-pre-hilbert-norm-on-schwartz-space]] and
[[lem-bessel-potential-norm-is-positive-definite]].

Concretely, its elements are equivalence classes $[u_j]$ of norm-Cauchy
sequences $(u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ in Schwartz space, where
$(u_j)\sim(v_j)$ exactly when
$\lim_{j\to\infty}q_s(u_j-v_j)=0$. The metric completion carries the unique
compatible Banach-space structure supplied by
[[def-completion-of-a-normed-space]] and
[[thm-metric-completion-carries-a-unique-banach-space-structure]]; its norm
is $\|[u_j]\|_{H^s}=\lim_j q_s(u_j)$. The constant-sequence map
$u\mapsto[(u,u,\ldots)]$ is the canonical dense linear isometry from Schwartz
space. At this definition stage $H^s$ is an abstract completion; no
identification with a subset of $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ is implicit.

The only choice assumption is Countable Choice, used by the cited metric
completion theorem in its countable-sequence construction and completeness
argument. No full Axiom of Choice or dependent choice is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ be the real-order Bessel-potential completion of
[[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] with its canonical embedding
$E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$
([[thm-bessel-potential-completions-embed-in-tempered-distributions]]). Write
$\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ for the Japanese bracket, $\mathcal F$
for the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, and
$u_g(\phi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}g(\xi)\phi(\xi)\,d\xi$ for the regular tempered
distribution of $g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Define
$$\mathcal W_s=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n):\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu=u_g \text{ in }\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)\text{ for some }g\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)\bigr\}.$$
Then:

1. The canonical embedding restricts to a bijection
   $E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal W_s$. Thus, after identifying a completion
   class with its image under $E_s$, $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ is **exactly** the set
   of tempered distributions whose bracket-weighted Fourier transform is the
   regular distribution of an $L^2$ class, and that class $g$ is unique.
2. The norm identity is exact:
$$\|U\|_{H^s}=\|g\|_2=\bigl\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)\bigr\|_2 \qquad(U\in H^s),$$
   where the last expression means the $L^2$ norm of the unique density $g$ of
   the distributional product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)$, and the
   defining completion norm $q_s(\phi)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat\phi\|_2$
   of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] is not renormalized.
3. The product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu$ is distributional
   multiplication of $\mathcal Fu$ by the smooth polynomially bounded bracket
   weight, not an a priori pointwise product; and $H^s$ elements are completion
   classes, not initially assumed to be functions.

Nothing here replaces the bracket weight by the Laplacian weight
$(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{s/2}$, and no pointwise value of $g$ at an individual
frequency is asserted before $g$ is obtained from the defining condition.

Assume countable choice (in particular, the Axiom of Choice suffices). Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $1\le p\le\infty$. Then
$L^p(\mu)$, with the norm of
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]], is

the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]].

Moreover, if a sequence in $L^p(\mu)$ converges in norm, then some subsequence
admits measurable representatives converging almost everywhere in the sense of

derivations.claim: First consider the hyperplane $\mathbb R^{d-1}\times\{0\}$ and $U\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$. Write $G(x')=U(x',0)$. Fourier inversion in the last coordinate and Fubini give $\widehat G(\xi')=\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat U(\xi',\eta)\,d\eta$.

Apply Cauchy–Schwarz with weights $\langle(\xi',\eta)\rangle^{s}$ and its reciprocal. The integral of the reciprocal square is $\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|\xi'|^2+\eta^2)^{-s}\,d\eta=C_s(1+|\xi'|^2)^{1/2-s}\le C_s,$ by the substitution $\eta=(1+|\xi'|^2)^{1/2}t$ and [A1]. Therefore $|\widehat G(\xi')|^2\le C_s\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|\xi'|^2+\eta^2)^s|\widehat U(\xi',\eta)|^2\,d\eta$. Integrating in $\xi'$ and applying [F1] proves $\|G\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^{d-1})}\le C_s\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}$.

Since Schwartz space is dense in the completion [F2], the estimate of step 2.1 makes the restrictions of every Cauchy representative a Cauchy sequence in $L^2$; completeness [F3] defines a bounded trace on the hyperplane. The same estimate applied to the difference of two representatives proves independence of the representative and linearity.

This trace is local. For $W\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)$, Fourier transformation in tangential variables and the weighted Cauchy--Schwarz estimate of step 2.1 give $\|W(\cdot,t)-W(\cdot,0)\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^{d-1})}^2\le\int_{\mathbb R^{d-1}}J_t(\xi')G(\xi')\,d\xi',$ where $J_t(\xi'):=\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|\xi'|^2+\eta^2)^{-s}|e^{2\pi i\eta t}-1|^2\,d\eta$ and $G(\xi'):=\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|\xi'|^2+\eta^2)^s|\widehat W(\xi',\eta)|^2\,d\eta$. For each $\xi'$, dominated convergence gives $J_t(\xi')\to0$ as $t\to0$, and $J_t(\xi')\le4C_s$ by step 2.1; $G$ is integrable by the definition of the $H^s$ norm. A second dominated-convergence argument therefore shows that the slices converge continuously in tangential $L^2$. If two extensions agree on $K$, their difference vanishes on an interior prism beside every relatively compact patch of $F$; taking a sequence $t_n\downarrow0$ from the full-measure set of zero interior slices shows their traces agree on that patch. A countable exhaustion covers $F$ up to its lower-dimensional boundary, which has surface measure zero. Hence the trace is independent of the extension. Translation and orthogonal changes of coordinates preserve both norms, so the hyperplane estimate from step 2.1 applies to the supporting plane of $F$ and then restricts to $F$.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix polynomial degree $k\ge0$, $1\le p,q\le\infty$, and integers
$0\le m\le\ell\le k$. Let the shape-regular affine simplex family be as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For every cell $K$ in that family,
there is a constant independent of cell size such that, for every
$v\in\mathbb P_k(K)$ and every facet $F\subset\partial K$,
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(K)} \le C h_K^{m-\ell+d(1/p-1/q)}|v|_{W^{m,q}(K)},$$
$$\|v\|_{L^p(F)} \le C h_K^{(d-1)/p-d/q}\|v\|_{L^q(K)}.$$
Use $1/\infty=0$. Constants may depend on $d,k,p,q$ and the family shape
regularity bound, but not on $K$ or $h_K$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge2$, a degree $k\ge1$, and a shape-regular matching affine simplicial mesh family as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. There is a selected constant $1\le C_{\mathrm{tr}}<\infty$, depending only on $d,k$ and the shape-regularity bound, such that for every cell $K$, every facet $F\subset\partial K$, and every scalar $v_h|_K\in\mathbb P_k(K)$,
$$h_F\|\partial_{n_{K,F}}v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C_{\mathrm{tr}}^2\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(K)}^2,$$
where $h_F=|K|/|F|$ and $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal of $K$ on $F$.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

derivations.claim: Sum [F1] over all boundary facets. Each cell contributes at most $N_\partial$ copies of its squared gradient norm, so $\sum_F h_F\|\partial_n v_h\|_F^2\le N_\partial C_{\mathrm{tr}}^2\sum_K\|\nabla v_h\|_K^2=N_\partial C_{\mathrm{tr}}^2\|\nabla v_h\|_\Omega^2$. Taking square roots proves the first inequality.

Choose a point $x_0$ in the interior of a mesh cell. The finite union of cells is compact and bounded, so the ray $x_0+tv$ has a last point in that union for every unit direction $v$. Choose $v$ outside the finitely many measure-zero sets of directions whose ray meets a cell face of dimension at most $d-2$ or is parallel to a facet plane; the excluded directions are measure zero because each such face has dimension at most $d-2$ and radial projection from $x_0$ has dimension at most $d-2$ on the $(d-1)$-sphere. The last point therefore lies in the relative interior of a facet and the ray crosses it transversally. If two cells meet at a point in the relative interior of a common facet, their interiors lie on opposite sides: if both lay on the same side of its affine hyperplane, a sufficiently small point displaced to that side near the facet point would lie in the interior of both nondegenerate simplices, contradicting their disjoint interiors in [F3]. Thus such a shared-facet point is interior to the union, contrary to its being the last point on the ray. The last point is consequently on a one-cell boundary facet. Since the local result gives $C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$, we obtain $1\le N_\partial$ and $C_\partial=\sqrt{N_\partial}C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$.

Apply [F4] on each facet and then finite-sum Cauchy–Schwarz to obtain $\left|\sum_F\int_F(\partial_n v_h)v_h\right|\le\sum_F(h_F^{1/2}\|\partial_n v_h\|_F)(h_F^{-1/2}\|v_h\|_F)\le\left(\sum_Fh_F\|\partial_n v_h\|_F^2\right)^{1/2}\left(\sum_Fh_F^{-1}\|v_h\|_F^2\right)^{1/2}.$ Substitute the first inequality from step 1.1 to get the stated bound.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected polyhedral open set, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Fix a polynomial degree $k\ge1$. Let $V_h$ be the real scalar conforming polynomial space of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], viewed as a subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]], and let $Y_h:=V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, where $H^1_0$ is the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; [[lem-nitsche-h-one-zero-functions-have-zero-facet-traces]] proves its facet-trace consequence. Boundary facets form $\mathcal F_h^\partial$. If $F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial$, let $K_F$ be its unique incident cell, $n_F$ its outward unit normal, $|F|$ its $(d-1)$-dimensional measure, and set $h_F:=|K_F|/|F|>0$. For functions with a defined boundary normal trace write $\partial_n v:=\nabla v\cdot n_F$ on $F$.

Let $\mathcal X_h$ consist of $v\in H^1(\Omega)$ such that for every cell $K$ there is $s_K>1/2$ with $v|_K\in H^{1+s_K}(K)$. By [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $v$ has an $L^2(F)$ trace on each facet, and each component of $\nabla(v|_K)$ is in $H^{s_K}(K)$, hence has an $L^2(F)$ trace by the same lemma; the derivative mapping follows from $|\xi_j|\langle\xi\rangle^{s_K}\le\langle\xi\rangle^{1+s_K}$ in the Bessel-potential norm. Thus $\partial_n v$ and all displayed integrals are defined. In particular, $V_h\subseteq\mathcal X_h$ and the exact/adjoint functions in the later regularity hypotheses lie in $\mathcal X_h$. For a dimensionless penalty coefficient $\gamma_0\ge0$ and symmetry parameter $\theta\in\{0,1\}$, define the same bilinear formula on $\mathcal X_h\times\mathcal X_h$:
$$a_h^\theta(v,w):=\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v)w\,dS-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fv(\partial_n w)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fvw\,dS.$$
For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ and boundary data $g$ with the displayed integrals finite, define
$$\ell_h^\theta(w_h):=\int_\Omega f w_h\,dx-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fg(\partial_n w_h)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fg w_h\,dS.$$
The **nonsymmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^0$; it has the consistency flux in the trial slot only. The **symmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^1$; it has both transposed consistency fluxes. The discrete weak-boundary problem is the standard Nitsche method when $\gamma_0>0$: it seeks $u_h\in V_h$ such that $a_h^\theta(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h^\theta(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$. This extension makes expressions such as $a_h^\theta(u,w_h)$ and $a_h^\theta(e,\zeta-z_h)$ well-defined when the exact and adjoint functions have the stated cellwise regularity. The boundary penalty is $\gamma_0/h_F$; $h_F$ is the cell-face height divided by $d$, not the face diameter. The zero value $\gamma_0=0$ is used only for the penalty-free algebraic comparison.

The energy seminorm and the comparison seminorm used below are
$$\|v\|_{E,h}^2:=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2,\qquad \|v\|_{\#,h}^2:=\|v\|_{E,h}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
These expressions are used only on functions for which their volume and facet traces are defined. The parameter $\theta$ fixes the sign convention; no convention based on a reciprocal small stabilization parameter is implicit.

Assume Countable Choice and the nonempty mesh hypotheses of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. Let $N_\partial$ be the maximum number of boundary facets incident to a single cell, and use the selected positive local constant $C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$ from [[lem-nitsche-local-polynomial-flux-inverse-trace]]. The mesh has at least one boundary facet, so $1\le N_\partial\le d+1$ and $C_\partial:=\sqrt{N_\partial}C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$. For every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad C_\partial:=\sqrt{N_\partial}\,C_{\mathrm{tr}}.$$
Consequently,
$$\left|\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v_h)v_h\,dS\right|\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
For simplices $N_\partial\le d+1$; no sharper face-count bound is needed.

By [F1] and [F2], $a_h^\theta(v_h,v_h)\ge x^2-(1+\theta)C_\partial xy+\gamma_0y^2.$ This is the quadratic form of the real symmetric matrix $M_\theta=\begin{pmatrix}1&-(1+\theta)C_\partial/2\\-(1+\theta)C_\partial/2&\gamma_0\end{pmatrix}$.

The eigenvalues of $M_\theta$ are $\frac{1+\gamma_0\pm\sqrt{(1-\gamma_0)^2+(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2}}2$, by the quadratic formula for its characteristic polynomial. Therefore $x^2-(1+\theta)C_\partial xy+\gamma_0y^2\ge\lambda_\theta(x^2+y^2)=\lambda_\theta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2$. Combine with step 1.1.

$$T_F:H^s(K)\longrightarrow L^2(F),\qquad \|T_Fv\|_{L^2(F)}\le C_s\|v\|_{H^s(K)},$$

$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad C_\partial:=\sqrt{N_\partial}\,C_{\mathrm{tr}}.$$
Consequently,
$$\left|\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v_h)v_h\,dS\right|\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
For simplices $N_\partial\le d+1$; no sharper face-count bound is needed.

Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]]. Put $C_\partial$ as in the latter item and let $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. If
$$\gamma_0>\frac{(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2}{4},$$
then for every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$a_h^\theta(v_h,v_h)\ge\lambda_\theta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2,\qquad \lambda_\theta:=\frac{1+\gamma_0-\sqrt{(1-\gamma_0)^2+(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2}}{2}>0.$$
Thus the sufficient threshold is $C_\partial^2/4$ for the nonsymmetric form and $C_\partial^2$ for the symmetric form. These are thresholds certified by the displayed inverse-trace bound, not asserted to be necessary for each individual mesh.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $r>1/2$, and let $q\in H^r(K;\mathbb R^d)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. Suppose $\operatorname{div}q\in L^2(K)$ distributionally. Then for every $v\in H^1(K)$,
$$\int_Kq\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\int_K(\operatorname{div}q)v\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(T_Fq\cdot n_{K,F})T_Fv\,dS,$$
where $T_Fq$ is the fractional $L^2(F)$ trace of [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $T_Fv$ is the weak $H^1$ endpoint trace of [[lem-nitsche-scaled-fractional-simplex-trace]] (agreeing with the Fourier trace whenever $v$ has a restriction-space extension), and $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal. This identifies the fractional facet trace of $q$ as its weak conormal flux.

Now let $\Omega$ be a nonempty bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$, let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ with $r>1/2$, and suppose $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ distributionally. The traces of $\nabla u$ from the two cells incident to every interior facet agree as vectors, so their outward normal fluxes cancel. For every $w\in H^1(\Omega)$ the sum of the cell identities is
$$\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F\partial_nu\,T_Fw\,dS=\int_\Omega fw\,dx.$$
Here $\mathcal F_h^\partial$ is the set of boundary facets, $\partial_nu:=T_F(\nabla u)\cdot n_F$, and all interior-facet value traces of a global $H^1(\Omega)$ function agree.

Let $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfy

$$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \varphi(x)\,dx = 1. $$

For $\varepsilon > 0$, define

$$ \varphi_\varepsilon(x) := \varepsilon^{-n}\varphi(x/\varepsilon) \qquad(x \in \mathbb{R}^n). $$

The family $(\varphi_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ is the **mollifier family
generated by $\varphi$**.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ be nonnegative with
$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\rho=1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$.
For $\varepsilon>0$ put $\rho_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-n}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$
and
$$\Omega_\varepsilon=\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^n\setminus\Omega)>\varepsilon\},\qquad\Omega_\varepsilon=\mathbb R^n\ \text{when }\Omega=\mathbb R^n .$$
Then $\rho_\varepsilon*u$ is defined and smooth on $\Omega_\varepsilon$, and
for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le k$,
$$D^\alpha(\rho_\varepsilon*u)=\rho_\varepsilon*(D^\alpha u)\qquad\text{on }\Omega_\varepsilon,$$
as pointwise smooth functions for the constructed representatives and as
almost-everywhere classes. Here $D^\alpha u$ is extended by zero off $\Omega$
in the convolution.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $(K_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ be an $L^1$ approximate identity on
$\mathbb{R}^n$. If $1 \le p < \infty$ and $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, then

$$\|f*K_\varepsilon - f\|_p \longrightarrow 0 \qquad(\varepsilon \to 0^+).$$

derivations.claim: The coercivity threshold in the Statement and [F3] give $a_h^\theta(v_h,v_h)\ge\lambda_\theta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2$ for all $v_h\in V_h$. If $\|v_h\|_{E,h}=0$, then the weak gradient of $v_h$ is zero. For any ball $B$ with $\overline B\subset\Omega$, take a slightly larger ball $B'$ still compactly contained in $\Omega$ and extend $v_h|_{B'}$ by zero. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, [F5] says its convolution agrees on $B$ with the local mollification of $v_h$ and has classical gradient zero there, so it is constant on $B$. Approximate-identity convergence in $L^2(B)$ makes these constants Cauchy and shows $v_h$ is a.e. constant on $B$. The points polygonally reachable from a fixed point form a nonempty open and relatively closed subset of connected $\Omega$: if a point of $\Omega$ is in the relative closure, a small ball in $\Omega$ meets the reachable set and its line segment reaches the point. Hence any two points are joined by a polygonal path. A compact polygonal path is covered by a finite chain of overlapping interior balls, so the local constants agree and give one a.e. constant $c$ on $\Omega$. On each cell its polynomial agrees a.e. with $c$ on the cell interior and therefore equals $c$ everywhere on the cell; its boundary trace is $c$. The global flux-bound supplier [F2] guarantees a boundary facet; that facet has positive measure and $h_F>0$, so the zero boundary term in $\|v_h\|_{E,h}$ forces $c=0$. Thus the energy seminorm is a norm on $V_h$.

The global identity [F4] gives $a_h^0(u,w_h)=\ell_h^0(w_h)$: its volume and first boundary-flux terms equal $(f,w_h)_\Omega$, and the penalty uses $g=u|_{\partial\Omega}$. For $\theta=1$, the additional term $-\sum_F\int_Fu\,\partial_nw_h$ equals the added load term $-\sum_F\int_Fg\,\partial_nw_h$, so $a_h^1(u,w_h)=\ell_h^1(w_h)$ as well. Subtracting the discrete equation yields $a_h^\theta(u-u_h^\theta,w_h)=0$ for all $w_h\in V_h$.

For any comparison function $z\in\mathcal X_h$ and any $w_h\in V_h$, weighted Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the four form terms by $|a_h^\theta(z,w_h)|\le(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)\|z\|_{\#,h}\|w_h\|_{\#,h}.$ Here the first flux term uses the flux component of $\|z\|_{\#,h}$ and the boundary-value component of $\|w_h\|_{\#,h}$; the transposed flux uses [F2] for $w_h$; the penalty uses the two boundary-value components. Also [F2] gives $\|w_h\|_{\#,h}^2\le(1+C_\partial^2)\|w_h\|_{E,h}^2$, so [F3] implies $a_h^\theta(w_h,w_h)\ge\alpha_\theta\|w_h\|_{\#,h}^2$ with $\alpha_\theta:=\lambda_\theta/(1+C_\partial^2)$.

Define the linear map $A_h:V_h\to V_h^*$ by $(A_hv_h)(w_h)=a_h^\theta(v_h,w_h)$. If $A_hv_h=0$, testing with $v_h$ and using [F3] gives $\lambda_\theta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2\le0$, hence $v_h=0$ by step 1.1. Therefore $A_h$ is injective; since $V_h$ and its dual are finite-dimensional with equal dimension, $A_h$ is bijective. The load $\ell_h^\theta$ is a finite linear functional on $V_h$, so the discrete equation has a unique solution.

Fix $v_h\in V_h$ and set $w_h:=u_h^\theta-v_h$. Step 1.2 gives $a_h^\theta(w_h,w_h)=a_h^\theta(u-v_h,w_h)$. By step 1.3, if $w_h\ne0$ then $\|w_h\|_{\#,h}\le\frac{(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)(1+C_\partial^2)}{\lambda_\theta}\|u-v_h\|_{\#,h};$ if $w_h=0$ the same inequality is immediate. The triangle inequality and infimum over $v_h$ prove the displayed quasi-optimal estimate. If [A2] holds, substituting its right-hand side proves the stated conditional rate.

Assume Countable Choice and the Poisson/Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] on a connected bounded polyhedral $\Omega$. Let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$, $r>1/2$, solve $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with Dirichlet trace $g$, and let $u_h^\theta$ solve the discrete problem for $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. Use the comparison seminorm $\|\cdot\|_{\#,h}$ of the definition. Put $C_\partial$ as in [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]], and assume
$$\gamma_0>(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2/4.$$
The discrete solution exists uniquely, and
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{\#,h},\qquad C_\theta:=1+\frac{(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)(1+C_\partial^2)}{\lambda_\theta},$$
where $\lambda_\theta$ is the positive coercivity constant in [[lem-nitsche-penalty-coercivity]]. If, in addition, the Nitsche comparison-norm approximation bound [A2] holds with exponent $t>0$, then
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta C_I\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K^{2t}\|u\|_{H^{1+t}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The result keeps the weak Dirichlet trace unconstrained in $V_h$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in the first slot, conjugate-linear in
the second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(u,v)|\le M\|u\|_V\|v\|_V.$$
$$\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)\ge\alpha\|u\|_V^2.$$
For every bounded linear functional $G:V\to\mathbb K$, there is a unique
$z\in V$ such that
$$a(v,z)=G(v)\qquad(v\in V),$$
and $\alpha\|z\|_V\le\|G\|_{V^*}$. In the real case conjugation is the
identity and both forms and functionals are linear over $\mathbb R$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $s\ge0$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty open set. Use $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ with the Bessel-potential completion convention of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Define the **restriction space**
$$H^s(D):=\{U|_D:U\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)\},\qquad \|u\|_{H^s(D)}:=\inf\{\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}:U|_D=u\text{ a.e. on }D\}.$$
Two extensions represent the same element exactly when their restrictions agree almost everywhere on $D$. This is the convention for fractional-order spaces on the polyhedral domain and its affine simplex cells used in the Nitsche items on this page. No $C^1$ boundary or trace theorem is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $n\ge1$ and
$s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ to be the normed-space completion
of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ with the positive-definite norm
$q_s(u)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat u\|_2$ from
[[def-bessel-potential-pre-hilbert-norm-on-schwartz-space]] and
[[lem-bessel-potential-norm-is-positive-definite]].

Concretely, its elements are equivalence classes $[u_j]$ of norm-Cauchy
sequences $(u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ in Schwartz space, where
$(u_j)\sim(v_j)$ exactly when
$\lim_{j\to\infty}q_s(u_j-v_j)=0$. The metric completion carries the unique
compatible Banach-space structure supplied by
[[def-completion-of-a-normed-space]] and
[[thm-metric-completion-carries-a-unique-banach-space-structure]]; its norm
is $\|[u_j]\|_{H^s}=\lim_j q_s(u_j)$. The constant-sequence map
$u\mapsto[(u,u,\ldots)]$ is the canonical dense linear isometry from Schwartz
space. At this definition stage $H^s$ is an abstract completion; no
identification with a subset of $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ is implicit.

The only choice assumption is Countable Choice, used by the cited metric
completion theorem in its countable-sequence construction and completeness
argument. No full Axiom of Choice or dependent choice is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ be the real-order Bessel-potential completion of
[[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] with its canonical embedding
$E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$
([[thm-bessel-potential-completions-embed-in-tempered-distributions]]). Write
$\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ for the Japanese bracket, $\mathcal F$
for the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, and
$u_g(\phi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}g(\xi)\phi(\xi)\,d\xi$ for the regular tempered
distribution of $g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Define
$$\mathcal W_s=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n):\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu=u_g \text{ in }\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)\text{ for some }g\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)\bigr\}.$$
Then:

1. The canonical embedding restricts to a bijection
   $E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal W_s$. Thus, after identifying a completion
   class with its image under $E_s$, $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ is **exactly** the set
   of tempered distributions whose bracket-weighted Fourier transform is the
   regular distribution of an $L^2$ class, and that class $g$ is unique.
2. The norm identity is exact:
$$\|U\|_{H^s}=\|g\|_2=\bigl\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)\bigr\|_2 \qquad(U\in H^s),$$
   where the last expression means the $L^2$ norm of the unique density $g$ of
   the distributional product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)$, and the
   defining completion norm $q_s(\phi)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat\phi\|_2$
   of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] is not renormalized.
3. The product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu$ is distributional
   multiplication of $\mathcal Fu$ by the smooth polynomially bounded bracket
   weight, not an a priori pointwise product; and $H^s$ elements are completion
   classes, not initially assumed to be functions.

Nothing here replaces the bracket weight by the Laplacian weight
$(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{s/2}$, and no pointwise value of $g$ at an individual
frequency is asserted before $g$ is obtained from the defining condition.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $F$ be one of its facets, and let $s>1/2$. Restriction of smooth functions has a unique bounded extension
$$T_F:H^s(K)\longrightarrow L^2(F),\qquad \|T_Fv\|_{L^2(F)}\le C_s\|v\|_{H^s(K)},$$
where $H^s(K)$ is the restriction space of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. The constant depends only on $s$ and the Fourier normalization, not on the location or orientation of the supporting hyperplane. If $V\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ is an extension of $v$, then $T_Fv$ is the restriction to $F$ of the unique $L^2$ hyperplane trace of $V$; hence it is independent of the chosen extension.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ have a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and let $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)=W^{1,2}_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ have the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]] and [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]. For every boundary facet $F\subset\partial K$ there is a bounded affine-simplex trace map $T_{K,F}:W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R)\to L^2(F;\mathbb R)$ agreeing with classical restriction on smooth functions. If $w\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, then $T_{K,F}(w|_K)=0$ in $L^2(F;\mathbb R)$. In particular, any globally $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ function that is polynomial on each cell and belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ has zero classical boundary restriction on every boundary facet.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $r>1/2$, and let $q\in H^r(K;\mathbb R^d)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. Suppose $\operatorname{div}q\in L^2(K)$ distributionally. Then for every $v\in H^1(K)$,
$$\int_Kq\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\int_K(\operatorname{div}q)v\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(T_Fq\cdot n_{K,F})T_Fv\,dS,$$
where $T_Fq$ is the fractional $L^2(F)$ trace of [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $T_Fv$ is the weak $H^1$ endpoint trace of [[lem-nitsche-scaled-fractional-simplex-trace]] (agreeing with the Fourier trace whenever $v$ has a restriction-space extension), and $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal. This identifies the fractional facet trace of $q$ as its weak conormal flux.

Now let $\Omega$ be a nonempty bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$, let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ with $r>1/2$, and suppose $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ distributionally. The traces of $\nabla u$ from the two cells incident to every interior facet agree as vectors, so their outward normal fluxes cancel. For every $w\in H^1(\Omega)$ the sum of the cell identities is
$$\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F\partial_nu\,T_Fw\,dS=\int_\Omega fw\,dx.$$
Here $\mathcal F_h^\partial$ is the set of boundary facets, $\partial_nu:=T_F(\nabla u)\cdot n_F$, and all interior-facet value traces of a global $H^1(\Omega)$ function agree.

Assume Countable Choice, $d\ge2$, a nonempty connected bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega$, a finite matching shape-regular affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$, and a polynomial degree $k\ge1$ as in [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. Put $h:=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K$ and $\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)$. For every $1/2<s\le1$ there is an explicitly defined linear map
$$I_{h,0}:H^{1+s}(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)\longrightarrow \mathbb P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)\subseteq Y_h$$
such that
$$\|\zeta-I_{h,0}\zeta\|_{\#,h}\le C h^s\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}=C_D h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad C_D:=C\ell_\Omega^{s-1}.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_{\#,h}$ and $Y_h=V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$ are exactly those of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. The constants are uniform over the mesh family and depend only on $d,s$ and its shape-regularity bound; the displayed conversion to $C_D$ uses the fixed nonempty domain. The construction uses cell means and affine reconstructions, never point values of $\zeta$. Its boundary-value error vanishes exactly. No approximation statement for higher polynomial degree or for nonzero-trace primal data is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice and the nonempty mesh hypotheses of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. Let $N_\partial$ be the maximum number of boundary facets incident to a single cell, and use the selected positive local constant $C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$ from [[lem-nitsche-local-polynomial-flux-inverse-trace]]. The mesh has at least one boundary facet, so $1\le N_\partial\le d+1$ and $C_\partial:=\sqrt{N_\partial}C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$. For every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad C_\partial:=\sqrt{N_\partial}\,C_{\mathrm{tr}}.$$
Consequently,
$$\left|\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v_h)v_h\,dS\right|\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
For simplices $N_\partial\le d+1$; no sharper face-count bound is needed.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected polyhedral open set, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Fix a polynomial degree $k\ge1$. Let $V_h$ be the real scalar conforming polynomial space of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], viewed as a subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]], and let $Y_h:=V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, where $H^1_0$ is the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; [[lem-nitsche-h-one-zero-functions-have-zero-facet-traces]] proves its facet-trace consequence. Boundary facets form $\mathcal F_h^\partial$. If $F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial$, let $K_F$ be its unique incident cell, $n_F$ its outward unit normal, $|F|$ its $(d-1)$-dimensional measure, and set $h_F:=|K_F|/|F|>0$. For functions with a defined boundary normal trace write $\partial_n v:=\nabla v\cdot n_F$ on $F$.

Let $\mathcal X_h$ consist of $v\in H^1(\Omega)$ such that for every cell $K$ there is $s_K>1/2$ with $v|_K\in H^{1+s_K}(K)$. By [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $v$ has an $L^2(F)$ trace on each facet, and each component of $\nabla(v|_K)$ is in $H^{s_K}(K)$, hence has an $L^2(F)$ trace by the same lemma; the derivative mapping follows from $|\xi_j|\langle\xi\rangle^{s_K}\le\langle\xi\rangle^{1+s_K}$ in the Bessel-potential norm. Thus $\partial_n v$ and all displayed integrals are defined. In particular, $V_h\subseteq\mathcal X_h$ and the exact/adjoint functions in the later regularity hypotheses lie in $\mathcal X_h$. For a dimensionless penalty coefficient $\gamma_0\ge0$ and symmetry parameter $\theta\in\{0,1\}$, define the same bilinear formula on $\mathcal X_h\times\mathcal X_h$:
$$a_h^\theta(v,w):=\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v)w\,dS-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fv(\partial_n w)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fvw\,dS.$$
For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ and boundary data $g$ with the displayed integrals finite, define
$$\ell_h^\theta(w_h):=\int_\Omega f w_h\,dx-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fg(\partial_n w_h)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fg w_h\,dS.$$
The **nonsymmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^0$; it has the consistency flux in the trial slot only. The **symmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^1$; it has both transposed consistency fluxes. The discrete weak-boundary problem is the standard Nitsche method when $\gamma_0>0$: it seeks $u_h\in V_h$ such that $a_h^\theta(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h^\theta(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$. This extension makes expressions such as $a_h^\theta(u,w_h)$ and $a_h^\theta(e,\zeta-z_h)$ well-defined when the exact and adjoint functions have the stated cellwise regularity. The boundary penalty is $\gamma_0/h_F$; $h_F$ is the cell-face height divided by $d$, not the face diameter. The zero value $\gamma_0=0$ is used only for the penalty-free algebraic comparison.

The energy seminorm and the comparison seminorm used below are
$$\|v\|_{E,h}^2:=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2,\qquad \|v\|_{\#,h}^2:=\|v\|_{E,h}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
These expressions are used only on functions for which their volume and facet traces are defined. The parameter $\theta$ fixes the sign convention; no convention based on a reciprocal small stabilization parameter is implicit.

Assume Countable Choice and the Poisson/Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] on a connected bounded polyhedral $\Omega$. Let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$, $r>1/2$, solve $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with Dirichlet trace $g$, and let $u_h^\theta$ solve the discrete problem for $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. Use the comparison seminorm $\|\cdot\|_{\#,h}$ of the definition. Put $C_\partial$ as in [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]], and assume
$$\gamma_0>(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2/4.$$
The discrete solution exists uniquely, and
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{\#,h},\qquad C_\theta:=1+\frac{(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)(1+C_\partial^2)}{\lambda_\theta},$$
where $\lambda_\theta$ is the positive coercivity constant in [[lem-nitsche-penalty-coercivity]]. If, in addition, the Nitsche comparison-norm approximation bound [A2] holds with exponent $t>0$, then
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta C_I\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K^{2t}\|u\|_{H^{1+t}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The result keeps the weak Dirichlet trace unconstrained in $V_h$.

derivations.claim: The adjoint equation is bounded and coercive on the Hilbert space $H^1_0(\Omega)$: Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the gradient form, and [F2] plus Poincaré makes it coercive in the usual $H^1$ norm. Its load $v\mapsto\int_\Omega ve$ is bounded by $\|v\|_{H^1}\|e\|_2$, so [F2] gives a unique weak solution; the stated higher regularity remains an assumption on this solution. Testing the adjoint equation with any $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)\subset H^1_0(\Omega)$ gives $\int\nabla\phi\cdot\nabla\zeta_e=\int\phi e$, exactly the distributional identity $-\Delta\zeta_e=e$. Thus [F6] applies to $\zeta_e$ as well as to $u$.

Apply [F6] to $\zeta_e$ with test $e$. The adjoint equation gives $\|e\|_2^2=\int_\Omega
abla e\cdot
abla\zeta_e-\sum_F\int_F e\,\partial_n\zeta_e$. By [F5], both $z_h$ and $\zeta_e$ have zero boundary traces, so $a_h^1(e,z_h)=0$ from [F1] reduces to $\int_\Omega
abla e\cdot
abla z_h-\sum_F\int_F e\,\partial_nz_h=0$; the other terms vanish because their test values are zero. Subtracting this zero identity yields $\|e\|_2^2=a_h^1(e,\zeta_e-z_h)$.

By [F3], the regularity of $u$ and $\zeta_e$ places $e$ and $\zeta_e-z_h$ in the comparison space $\mathcal X_h$ of the forms definition; [F4] supplies their facet traces. For arbitrary $v,w\in\mathcal X_h$, weighted Cauchy–Schwarz in the form definition bounds the volume product by $\|v\|_{\#,h}\|w\|_{\#,h}$, each of the two flux products by the product of the normal-flux component of one norm and the boundary-value component of the other, and the penalty product by $\gamma_0\|v\|_{\#,h}\|w\|_{\#,h}$. Thus $|a_h^1(v,w)|\le(3+\gamma_0)\|v\|_{\#,h}\|w\|_{\#,h}$. By [F8], $C_\partial\ge1$, so $3+\gamma_0\le2+C_\partial+\gamma_0=M_1$. This proves the all-comparison-space bound with the original $M_1$, without applying a discrete inverse estimate to $\zeta_e-z_h$.

Interpolation [F7] and the bound of step 1.3 give $\|e\|_2^2=|a_h^1(e,\zeta_e-z_h)|\le M_1C_Dh^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|e\|_{\#,h}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}}$. Use [A1]; if $\|e\|_2=0$ the conclusion is immediate, and otherwise divide by $\|e\|_2$ to obtain the first estimate.

Under the separate higher-order primal hypothesis [A3], substitute its energy error bound into the first estimate from step 2.1 and multiply the constants. This gives the stated conditional primal $L^2$ rate without changing its exponent range or local seminorm.

Let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$, $r>1/2$, solve $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with Dirichlet trace $g$, and let $u_h^\theta$ solve the discrete problem for $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. $$\gamma_0>(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2/4.$$

$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{\#,h},\qquad C_\theta:=1+\frac{(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)(1+C_\partial^2)}{\lambda_\theta},$$
where $\lambda_\theta$ is the positive coercivity constant in [[lem-nitsche-penalty-coercivity]]. If, in addition, the Nitsche comparison-norm approximation bound [A2] holds with exponent $t>0$, then

The result keeps the weak Dirichlet trace unconstrained in $V_h$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in the first slot, conjugate-linear in
the second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(u,v)|\le M\|u\|_V\|v\|_V.$$
$$\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)\ge\alpha\|u\|_V^2.$$
For every bounded linear functional $G:V\to\mathbb K$, there is a unique
$z\in V$ such that
$$a(v,z)=G(v)\qquad(v\in V),$$
and $\alpha\|z\|_V\le\|G\|_{V^*}$. In the real case conjugation is the
identity and both forms and functionals are linear over $\mathbb R$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $s\ge0$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty open set. Use $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ with the Bessel-potential completion convention of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Define the **restriction space**
$$H^s(D):=\{U|_D:U\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)\},\qquad \|u\|_{H^s(D)}:=\inf\{\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}:U|_D=u\text{ a.e. on }D\}.$$
Two extensions represent the same element exactly when their restrictions agree almost everywhere on $D$. This is the convention for fractional-order spaces on the polyhedral domain and its affine simplex cells used in the Nitsche items on this page. No $C^1$ boundary or trace theorem is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $n\ge1$ and
$s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ to be the normed-space completion
of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ with the positive-definite norm
$q_s(u)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat u\|_2$ from
[[def-bessel-potential-pre-hilbert-norm-on-schwartz-space]] and
[[lem-bessel-potential-norm-is-positive-definite]].

Concretely, its elements are equivalence classes $[u_j]$ of norm-Cauchy
sequences $(u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ in Schwartz space, where
$(u_j)\sim(v_j)$ exactly when
$\lim_{j\to\infty}q_s(u_j-v_j)=0$. The metric completion carries the unique
compatible Banach-space structure supplied by
[[def-completion-of-a-normed-space]] and
[[thm-metric-completion-carries-a-unique-banach-space-structure]]; its norm
is $\|[u_j]\|_{H^s}=\lim_j q_s(u_j)$. The constant-sequence map
$u\mapsto[(u,u,\ldots)]$ is the canonical dense linear isometry from Schwartz
space. At this definition stage $H^s$ is an abstract completion; no
identification with a subset of $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ is implicit.

The only choice assumption is Countable Choice, used by the cited metric
completion theorem in its countable-sequence construction and completeness
argument. No full Axiom of Choice or dependent choice is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge1$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ be the real-order Bessel-potential completion of
[[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] with its canonical embedding
$E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$
([[thm-bessel-potential-completions-embed-in-tempered-distributions]]). Write
$\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ for the Japanese bracket, $\mathcal F$
for the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, and
$u_g(\phi)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}g(\xi)\phi(\xi)\,d\xi$ for the regular tempered
distribution of $g\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Define
$$\mathcal W_s=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n):\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu=u_g \text{ in }\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)\text{ for some }g\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)\bigr\}.$$
Then:

1. The canonical embedding restricts to a bijection
   $E_s:H^s(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathcal W_s$. Thus, after identifying a completion
   class with its image under $E_s$, $H^s(\mathbb R^n)$ is **exactly** the set
   of tempered distributions whose bracket-weighted Fourier transform is the
   regular distribution of an $L^2$ class, and that class $g$ is unique.
2. The norm identity is exact:
$$\|U\|_{H^s}=\|g\|_2=\bigl\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)\bigr\|_2 \qquad(U\in H^s),$$
   where the last expression means the $L^2$ norm of the unique density $g$ of
   the distributional product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal F(E_sU)$, and the
   defining completion norm $q_s(\phi)=\|\langle\xi\rangle^s\widehat\phi\|_2$
   of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]] is not renormalized.
3. The product $\langle\xi\rangle^s\mathcal Fu$ is distributional
   multiplication of $\mathcal Fu$ by the smooth polynomially bounded bracket
   weight, not an a priori pointwise product; and $H^s$ elements are completion
   classes, not initially assumed to be functions.

Nothing here replaces the bracket weight by the Laplacian weight
$(1+4\pi^2|\xi|^2)^{s/2}$, and no pointwise value of $g$ at an individual
frequency is asserted before $g$ is obtained from the defining condition.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $F$ be one of its facets, and let $s>1/2$. Restriction of smooth functions has a unique bounded extension
$$T_F:H^s(K)\longrightarrow L^2(F),\qquad \|T_Fv\|_{L^2(F)}\le C_s\|v\|_{H^s(K)},$$
where $H^s(K)$ is the restriction space of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. The constant depends only on $s$ and the Fourier normalization, not on the location or orientation of the supporting hyperplane. If $V\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ is an extension of $v$, then $T_Fv$ is the restriction to $F$ of the unique $L^2$ hyperplane trace of $V$; hence it is independent of the chosen extension.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ have a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and let $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)=W^{1,2}_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ have the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]] and [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]. For every boundary facet $F\subset\partial K$ there is a bounded affine-simplex trace map $T_{K,F}:W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R)\to L^2(F;\mathbb R)$ agreeing with classical restriction on smooth functions. If $w\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, then $T_{K,F}(w|_K)=0$ in $L^2(F;\mathbb R)$. In particular, any globally $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ function that is polynomial on each cell and belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ has zero classical boundary restriction on every boundary facet.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $r>1/2$, and let $q\in H^r(K;\mathbb R^d)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. Suppose $\operatorname{div}q\in L^2(K)$ distributionally. Then for every $v\in H^1(K)$,
$$\int_Kq\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\int_K(\operatorname{div}q)v\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(T_Fq\cdot n_{K,F})T_Fv\,dS,$$
where $T_Fq$ is the fractional $L^2(F)$ trace of [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $T_Fv$ is the weak $H^1$ endpoint trace of [[lem-nitsche-scaled-fractional-simplex-trace]] (agreeing with the Fourier trace whenever $v$ has a restriction-space extension), and $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal. This identifies the fractional facet trace of $q$ as its weak conormal flux.

Now let $\Omega$ be a nonempty bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$, let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ with $r>1/2$, and suppose $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ distributionally. The traces of $\nabla u$ from the two cells incident to every interior facet agree as vectors, so their outward normal fluxes cancel. For every $w\in H^1(\Omega)$ the sum of the cell identities is
$$\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F\partial_nu\,T_Fw\,dS=\int_\Omega fw\,dx.$$

$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an affine bijection from a bounded open
set $\widehat K\subset\mathbb R^d$ to $K$, where $A$ is invertible, and let
$1\le p\le\infty$. For every integer $r\ge0$ and scalar
$v\in W^{r,p}(K)$, the pullback $\widehat v:=v\circ F$ belongs to
$W^{r,p}(\widehat K)$. For $r\ge1$ its first weak derivatives satisfy
$$D_{\widehat x_j}\widehat v=\sum_{i=1}^d A_{ij}(D_{x_i}v)\circ F,$$
and higher derivatives are obtained by applying this constant-matrix rule
repeatedly. In particular, for each $0\le m\le r$,
$$|\widehat v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat K)}\le C(d,m)\|A\|^m|\det A|^{-1/p}|v|_{W^{m,p}(K)},$$
where $|\det A|^{-1/p}:=1$ for $p=\infty$. The reverse estimate holds
with $A^{-1}$ and $|\det A|^{1/p}$ in place of $A$ and
$|\det A|^{-1/p}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex and let
$G\in C^1(\overline K;\mathbb R^d)$. If $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit
normal on each facet $F$, then
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_FG\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS.$$
For an orientation-preserving affine map $F_K(\widehat x)=b+A\widehat x$,
the oriented area element transforms as
$$n_{K,F}\,dS=\det(A)A^{-T}\widehat n_{\widehat F}\,d\widehat S.$$

Assume Countable Choice, as in
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and
[[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]]. For an open set
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, an integer $k\ge0$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, set
$$H^k(\Omega;\mathbb K):=W^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The elements are the same almost-everywhere classes, and their weak
derivatives and norm are exactly those already defined for $W^{k,2}$. When the
scalar field is fixed, write $H^k(\Omega)$.

The notation $H^k_0(\Omega)$ is reserved for the later definition by closure of
compactly supported smooth functions in the Sobolev norm. This item assigns no
boundary values to an equivalence class and asserts no characterization by
pointwise vanishing or by traces.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ be the reference map and let $\widehat w=w\circ F_K$. By [F2], $\widehat w\in W^{1,2}(\widehat S_d)$ and its norm is bounded by a finite constant depending on $A_K$ times $\|w\|_{W^{1,2}(K)}$. The surface Jacobian $J_F$ is positive and constant by [F3]. Define $T_{K,F}w$ by pullback of $\gamma_{\widehat F}\widehat w$; then $$\|T_{K,F}w\|_{L^2(F)}^2=J_F\|\gamma_{\widehat F}\widehat w\|_{L^2(\widehat F)}^2\le J_F C_{\widehat F}^2\|\widehat w\|_{W^{1,2}(\widehat S_d)}^2\le C_{K,F}^2\|w\|_{W^{1,2}(K)}^2.$$ Thus the trace is bounded, and it agrees with ordinary restriction for smooth $w$ by [F1].

Let $w\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. For each $m\ge1$, the closure property [F4] and Countable Choice [F5] give $\phi_m\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with $\|w-\phi_m\|_{W^{1,2}(\Omega)}<1/m$. Restriction to $K$ cannot increase this norm, so step 1.1 gives $$\|T_{K,F}(w|_K)-T_{K,F}(\phi_m|_K)\|_{L^2(F)}\le C_{K,F}/m.$$ The support of each $\phi_m$ is compactly contained in $\Omega$, hence $\phi_m$ vanishes in a neighborhood of the boundary facet $F$ and its trace is zero by step 1.1. Letting $m\to\infty$ proves $T_{K,F}(w|_K)=0$.

If $p$ is polynomial on $K$, then it is smooth and step 1.1 identifies $T_{K,F}(p)$ with its classical restriction. Therefore for a global piecewise-polynomial $p\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, step 2.1 makes that restriction zero on each boundary facet. This proves the final assertion.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 proves the trace is zero by taking the limit of zero traces of compactly supported smooth approximants.

The matching affine mesh requires nondegenerate simplices.
The trace result has no real parameter interval or endpoint case.
